html:
The Old Prussians were a Baltic people on the southeast coast of the Baltic Sea, between the Vistula and the Neman. They are on the map for 1000 and 1100.

They were one of the Baltic peoples. They lived in clans and districts, gathered amber on their shores, and worshipped their own gods in sacred groves. They fought off Christian missions: in 997 they killed the missionary bishop Adalbert of Prague, who had come with Polish support.

In the 1220s a Polish duke invited the Teutonic Knights to fight them. In the Northern Crusades the knights conquered Prussia by 1283 after long wars and great revolts, and settled German farmers there. The Prussian language died out around 1700, but the name passed to the German state of Prussia.
sum: The Old Prussians were a Baltic people on the southeast coast of the Baltic Sea, between the Vistula and the Neman. They are on the map for 1000 and 1100.
